proposal.action: Adopt binding staged production/consumption controls with differentiated implementation and periodic review.
proposal.purpose: reduce a serious plausible long-lived global atmospheric risk while allowing transition and evidence-based adjustment
proposal.requested_authority: Adopt binding staged production/consumption controls with differentiated implementation and periodic review.

evidence.claim: Scientific work identifies a credible chemical mechanism by which the long-lived industrial substances reach the upper atmosphere and catalytically damage the protective layer.
Recent ground observations show an unexpectedly severe recurring regional depletion of the protective layer.
Additional observations/analysis support that the phenomenon is real and linked to the relevant chemistry, while details/global extrapolation remain under refinement.
Damage to the protective layer increases biologically harmful radiation at the surface, creating plausible serious health/ecological risks even though exact future incidence is uncertain.
The substances are long-lived and globally mixed, so benefits of use can be local/immediate while risks are exported geographically and temporally.
Controls impose genuine industrial/consumer costs because the substances have valuable uses and substitute technologies are unevenly mature.
An existing international framework already supports research/monitoring but does not impose the binding reductions now under consideration.
A staged agreement can target major substances first, differentiate lower-capacity implementation and mandate periodic science/economic assessment so controls can change with evidence.
Waiting for precise proof allows additional long-lived pollutant accumulation, making later reversal slower if stronger evidence emerges.

affected_parties.party: current/future populations exposed if the atmospheric protection system degrades
affected_parties.interests_or_risks: Health consequences of increased harmful radiation and related environmental effects.
Inherited long-lived atmospheric damage created before they can influence decisions.
Investment, jobs, product performance and transition/retooling costs.
Price, availability, safety and reliable substitutes.
Development, technology access and avoiding disproportionate transition burdens for a globally generated problem.

alternatives.description: Use voluntary industry/national targets while research continues.
Delay binding controls until future harm and industrial alternatives are much more certain.
Impose an immediate near-total ban regardless of substitution feasibility/capacity.
Combine staged controls with financial/technical cooperation for lower-capacity countries.
Binding initial controls on the highest-risk chemicals with periodic reassessment.
Staged controls plus finance/technology support for lower-capacity states.
No binding controls until substantially greater certainty.

uncertainties: Exact future global/regional depletion under alternative emissions paths.
Exact downstream health/ecological burden and timing.
Cost/safety/technical maturity of substitutes in every application.
Transition speed without major supply/price disruption.
Fair burden allocation across differently responsible/capable states.
Whether initial staged reductions will be sufficient or later need strengthening.
requested_capability: Adopt binding staged production/consumption controls with differentiated implementation and periodic review.
